ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$5.92 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7 form) for the unexempted detour mileage, and remind the driver of the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation; no account flag is warranted.

segment_findings.reason: Detour on Tampines Avenue 12 (09:03:20-09:03:50, ~0.6 km extra). The driver's congestion excuse (RD-4) fails: the only traffic incident (Accident, 08:44, 1.38075/103.91929) lies on the route the driver actually drove, not on the replaced optimal segment (TAMPINES EXPRESSWAY section per the quoted polyline, ~0.5 km away), and the SYN-1005 speed band covers the traversed section, not the replaced one; RD-4(a) requires the corroboration to target the replaced optimal segment. Band evidence alone is insufficient per RD-4(b)/G3. No chat agreement to this diversion (chat only covers pickup logistics), so RD-5 does not exempt it.

Detour around the Tampines Ave 12 / Tampines Expressway ramp area (09:04:20-09:04:50, ~0.4 km extra) recovering toward the optimal route. Same RD-4 failure: the 08:44 Accident and the band-1 record attach to the driven Expressway segment (1.3803/103.9198), not to the replaced optimal segment (~1.3846/103.9162, ~0.5 km away). No prior passenger consent in chat (RD-5).

rejected_claims.reason: RD-4 not satisfied: the accident/band evidence is located on the route actually driven, ~0.5 km from the optimal segment it purportedly replaced, so it does not justify the deviation. RD-4(b) band evidence cannot exempt on its own (G3).

Accepted in part: no chat evidence of any agreed route change (RD-5), so nothing is exempted on consent grounds; however the fare excess is limited to detour mileage actually driven (1.8 km), not the full meter-vs-quote difference.
